name: Bento Grid
hint: Move across the tiles: one light follows you and the tile you approach starts playing. Click a tile to open it.
description: A features section of tiles in an asymmetric bento grid. You pass the tiles: a title, a line of copy, an optional tag, any node as the tile's visual, a size (small, wide, tall, hero or an explicit span) and an href or a click handler; a tile with a `panel` grows over the grid into that panel when opened, and Esc returns it. One pointer light (a single SVG gradient driven by motion values) crosses the whole grid and lights the borders of nearby tiles. With `demo` it shows the sample, set in an incident-response tool, where every tile is a small working demo instead of an icon and a paragraph: an alert is acknowledged and resolved, a latency line crosses its threshold and pages someone, a rota hands over on the hour, a command types itself, sources wire up, a status page flips to Operational; the tile you approach blooms into colour and plays, and each one opens into a hands-on version of itself. The layout follows the section's own width: 4 columns, 3, 2, or a phone stack where small tiles sit two-across.
intents: bento grid features section for a landing page
mosaic of animated feature cards, each one a live product demo
asymmetric feature grid with a hover spotlight glow
feature card that expands into an interactive detail view
show what a SaaS product does on a marketing page
usage: Use once per landing page as the features section, after the hero. Pass `items`: one feature per tile with an `id`, a `title` of a few words, a one-line `body`, a `visual` node (a screenshot, a chart, a small live demo) and a `size`; keep one tile `hero` and the rest quieter. Six or seven tiles is the limit. Make a tile a link with `href`, a button with `onClick` (or `onItemClick` for all tiles), or give it a `panel` node to open it over the grid; read or drive the open tile with `expanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange`. Add `eyebrow`, `heading` and `intro` for the header. Tiles flow in the order given (row by row, no reordering), so plan the sizes to fill each row. With no `items` it shows nothing (or only the header you pass).

dataProps.description: The tiles, in reading order. `size` sets the span (small 1×1, wide 2×1, tall 1×2, hero 2×2; `span` overrides it, clamped to the columns showing). The whole tile is the link (`href`) or button (`onClick`, `onItemClick`, or a `panel` to open). `tag` shows on wide and hero tiles. Empty shows no grid.
